answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities to a quadratic stake-slashing mechanism. When transactions flow like a river across the network, validating nodes deposit collateral into a cryptographic stake burning contract. Fees scale as a superlinear function, O(N^2), forcing each added clone over the initial threshold knoll to incur exponentially escalating burning penalties. This dynamic fee terrace ensures attacker cost scales superlinearly, making mass identity replication economically catastrophic.
